title: Spring-Alameda Safety & Mobility Project 9/10/26
description:
Los Angeles city leaders officially broke ground on the Spring Alameda Safety and Mobility Project. This major street overhaul transforms a 1.2-mile stretch connecting Chinatown, Union Station, and the LA State Historic Park into a safer, more accessible space for everyone.

Between 2013 and 2022, vehicles struck 46 pedestrians and cyclists along this high-risk corridor. To prevent future traffic violence, city crews are adding protected bike lanes, rebuilt curb ramps, high-visibility crosswalks, and two new pedestrian signals.

More than 2,000 community members helped design the new features. These additions will make walking and biking safer for families, local seniors, and transit riders accessing parks and neighboring businesses.

Work is already underway, with full completion expected by early next summer. These infrastructure upgrades will serve local neighborhoods for generations, long after the 2028 Olympic Games conclude.
